rules.rule_name: Close Account Master File After Full Processing
rules.rule_description: The Account Master File must be formally closed once all account records have been read and processed. This ensures all data is properly finalized and system resources are released.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Close Account Master File

acceptance_criteria.Given: All account records from the Account Master File have been read and processed successfully
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initiates the closure of the Account Master File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account Master File is closed successfully, confirming that all account records have been fully processed and the file is properly finalized

rules.rule_name: Validate Successful Closure of Account Master File
rules.rule_description: After attempting to close the Account Master File, the program must verify that the closure was completed successfully. If the file did not close properly, the program must terminate with an error to prevent data integrity issues.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: File Closed Successfully?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has attempted to close the Account Master File after processing all account records
acceptance_criteria.When: The file closure status is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the file closed successfully, processing is marked as complete and the program continues to normal termination; if the file did not close successfully, an 'ERROR CLOSING ACCOUNT FILE' message is displayed, the error status is recorded, and the program terminates abnormally

rules.rule_name: Confirm All Account Records Have Been Processed
rules.rule_description: Upon successful closure of the Account Master File, the program confirms that all account records have been fully processed, including transformation and writing to all output files.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: All Account Records Have Been Processed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Master File has been closed successfully
acceptance_criteria.When: The file closure is confirmed as successful
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program acknowledges that all account records have been processed and proceeds to normal program end, displaying 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT01C'

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program CBACT01C is starting execution and the Account Master File (ACCTFILE-FILE) is available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Account Master File for input reading
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Master File is successfully opened and the program proceeds to open the Output Account File; if the file cannot be opened, the program displays 'ERROR OPENING ACCTFILE' and terminates abnormally

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Account Master File for Reading
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program must successfully open the Account Master File as an input source before any account records can be read and processed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Master File has been successfully opened and the Output Account File (OUT-FILE) is available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Output Account File for writing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Output Account File is successfully opened and the program proceeds to open the Array Output File; if the file cannot be opened, the program displays 'ERROR OPENING OUTFILE' along with the file status and terminates abnormally

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Output Account File for Writing
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program must successfully open the Output Account File as a write destination before any transformed account records can be written.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Output Account File has been successfully opened and the Array Output File (ARRY-FILE) is available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Array Output File for writing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Array Output File is successfully opened and the program proceeds to open the Variable-Length Record File; if the file cannot be opened, the program displays 'ERROR OPENING ARRAYFILE' along with the file status and terminates abnormally

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Array Output File for Writing
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program must successfully open the Array Output File as a write destination before any account balance array records can be written.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Array Output File has been successfully opened and the Variable-Length Record File (VBRC-FILE) is available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Variable-Length Record File for writing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Variable-Length Record File is successfully opened and the program proceeds to the main account processing loop; if the file cannot be opened, the program displays 'ERROR OPENING VBRC FILE' along with the file status and terminates abnormally

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Variable-Length Record File for Writing
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program must successfully open the Variable-Length Record File as a write destination before any short or long variable-length records can be written.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Master File is open for input and the end-of-file condition has not yet been reached
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reads the next account record from the Account Master File into the ACCOUNT-RECORD area
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the read is successful, the account record fields (Account ID, Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Open Date, Expiration Date, Reissue Date, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Group ID) are available for processing; if end-of-file is detected, the end-of-file flag is set to 'Y' and the loop terminates; if any other read error occurs, the program displays 'ERROR READING ACCOUNT FILE' and terminates abnormally

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Next Account Record from Account Master File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program sequentially reads each account record from the Account Master File into the Account Record working area for processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been successfully read from the Account Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program processes the account record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following fields are displayed on the console: Account ID (ACCT-ID), Active Status (ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS), Current Balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL), Credit Limit (ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT), Cash Credit Limit (ACCT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT), Open Date (ACCT-OPEN-DATE), Expiration Date (ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE), Reissue Date (ACCT-REISSUE-DATE), Current Cycle Credit (ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT), Current Cycle Debit (ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT), and Group ID (ACCT-GROUP-ID), followed by a separator line

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Account Record Details to Console
all_rules.Rule_Description: For every account record successfully read, all key account fields are displayed to the console output for visibility and audit purposes before any transformation is applied.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been read and the Account Reissue Date (ACCT-REISSUE-DATE) is available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program prepares the output account record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Reissue Date is passed to the external date conversion routine COBDATFT with input format type '2' and output format type '2'; the converted date returned in CODATECN-0UT-DATE is stored as the output reissue date (OUT-ACCT-REISSUE-DATE); the original reissue date is also preserved in WS-REISSUE-DATE for subsequent use in variable-length record population

all_rules.Rule_Name: Convert Account Reissue Date Format
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Reissue Date must be converted from its source format to the required output format using the external date conversion service before being written to the Output Account File.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record is being prepared for output and the Current Cycle Debit field (ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT) has been evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The value of ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT is equal to zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The output Current Cycle Debit field (OUT-ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT) is set to the default value of 2525.00; when ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT is non-zero, the actual value from the account record is carried forward as-is to the output

all_rules.Rule_Name: Apply Default Current Cycle Debit When Zero
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account has no current cycle debit activity (zero value), a standard default debit amount of 2525.00 must be applied to the output record to ensure the field is never left at zero in the output.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been read, the reissue date has been converted, and the cycle debit default rule has been evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program populates the output account record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following fields are mapped directly from input to output: Account ID, Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Open Date, Expiration Date, Current Cycle Credit, and Group ID; the Reissue Date is set to the converted date value; the Current Cycle Debit is set to 2525.00 if the input was zero, otherwise the input value is used

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Output Account Record Fields
all_rules.Rule_Description: All account fields are mapped from the input Account Master Record to the Output Account Record, applying the reissue date conversion result and the cycle debit default rule before writing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The output account record (OUT-ACCT-REC) has been fully populated with all transformed field values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program writes the output account record to the Output Account File (OUT-FILE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The record is successfully written to the Output Account File and processing continues to populate the Array Record; if the write operation fails, the program displays 'ACCOUNT FILE WRITE STATUS IS:' followed by the file status code and terminates abnormally

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Transformed Account Record to Output File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The fully populated and transformed output account record must be written to the Output Account File.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been successfully read and the Output Account Record has been written
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program populates the Account Balance Array Record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID (ACCT-ID) is set as the array record identifier; Slot 1 is populated with the actual Account Current Balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL) and a fixed Current Cycle Debit of 1005.00; Slot 2 is populated with the actual Account Current Balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL) and a fixed Current Cycle Debit of 1525.00; Slot 3 is populated with a fixed balance of -1025.00 and a fixed Current Cycle Debit of -2500.00 regardless of actual account values; the array record is initialized (cleared) before population for each account

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Account Balance Array Record with Three Fixed Slots
all_rules.Rule_Description: For each account, an array record containing three balance and debit slots is created. Slots 1 and 2 carry the actual account current balance with fixed predetermined debit amounts, while slot 3 always carries fixed negative values representing a standard adjustment entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Balance Array Record (ARR-ARRAY-REC) has been fully populated with the Account ID and three balance/debit slots
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program writes the array record to the Array Output File (ARRY-FILE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The array record is successfully written to the Array Output File and processing continues to populate the variable-length records; if the write operation fails, the program displays 'ACCOUNT FILE WRITE STATUS IS:' followed by the file status and terminates abnormally

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Account Balance Array Record to Array File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The populated three-slot account balance array record must be written to the Array Output File.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been processed and the Array Record has been written; the variable-length record area (VBRC-REC1) has been initialized (cleared)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program populates the short variable-length record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID (ACCT-ID) is mapped to VB1-ACCT-ID and the Account Active Status (ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS) is mapped to VB1-ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS; this record is designated as 12 bytes in length for writing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Short Variable-Length Record with Account Identity Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: A short 12-byte variable-length record is created per account containing only the account identity fields: Account ID and Active Status.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been processed and the short variable-length record has been populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program populates the long variable-length record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID (ACCT-ID) is mapped to VB2-ACCT-ID; the Current Balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL) is mapped to VB2-ACCT-CURR-BAL; the Credit Limit (ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT) is mapped to VB2-ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT; the Reissue Year portion (WS-ACCT-REISSUE-YYYY) extracted from the stored reissue date is mapped to VB2-ACCT-REISSUE-YYYY; this record is designated as 39 bytes in length for writing; both VB records are displayed on the console before writing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Long Variable-Length Record with Account Financial Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: A long 39-byte variable-length record is created per account containing the account's financial details: Account ID, Current Balance, Credit Limit, and the Reissue Year.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The short variable-length record (VBRC-REC1) has been populated with Account ID and Active Status
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program writes the short variable-length record to the Variable-Length Record File (VBRC-FILE) with a record length of 12 bytes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The 12-byte record is successfully written to the Variable-Length Record File and processing continues to write the long variable-length record; if the write operation fails, the program displays 'ACCOUNT FILE WRITE STATUS IS:' followed by the file status and terminates abnormally

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Short Variable-Length Record to Variable-Length File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The 12-byte short variable-length record containing account identity data must be written to the Variable-Length Record File.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The long variable-length record (VBRC-REC2) has been populated with Account ID, Current Balance, Credit Limit, and Reissue Year
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program writes the long variable-length record to the Variable-Length Record File (VBRC-FILE) with a record length of 39 bytes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The 39-byte record is successfully written to the Variable-Length Record File and the loop returns to check for the next account record; if the write operation fails, the program displays 'ACCOUNT FILE WRITE STATUS IS:' followed by the file status and terminates abnormally

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Long Variable-Length Record to Variable-Length File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The 39-byte long variable-length record containing account financial details must be written to the Variable-Length Record File.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is in the main account processing loop
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The end-of-file condition is evaluated after each read attempt
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If end-of-file has not been reached (END-OF-FILE = 'N'), the program reads and processes the next account record; if end-of-file has been reached (END-OF-FILE = 'Y'), the loop terminates and the program proceeds to close the Account Master File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Control Account Record Processing Loop Until End of File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program must continue processing account records one at a time until all records in the Account Master File have been read and processed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All account records have been read from the Account Master File and the end-of-file condition has been reached
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program closes the Account Master File (ACCTFILE-FILE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Master File is successfully closed and the program displays 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT01C' and terminates normally; if the file cannot be closed, the program displays 'ERROR CLOSING ACCOUNT FILE' and terminates abnormally

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Account Master File After All Records Processed
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all account records have been read and processed, the Account Master File must be properly closed to complete the program execution.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The batch account processing program CBACT01C is starting execution and the Account Master File is available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initiates the opening of the Account Master File in sequential read (input) mode as the very first operation before any account record processing begins
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Master File is opened successfully in sequential read mode and is ready for record-by-record processing of all account records

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Master File Must Be Opened Before Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Master File must be successfully opened in sequential read mode as the first step before any account records can be read or processed. This ensures all account data is accessible for the batch run.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to open the Account Master File in sequential read mode
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file open operation completes and the resulting file status is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file status indicates success (status = '00'), the Account Master File is confirmed as ready for processing and the program proceeds to read account records; otherwise the program treats the open as a failure

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Master File Open Success Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to open the Account Master File, the program must verify that the file was opened successfully. A successful open is the only condition under which account record processing is permitted to proceed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to open the Account Master File in sequential read mode
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file open operation results in a status other than success (status not equal to '00')
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program displays the error message 'ERROR OPENING ACCTFILE' along with the file status details, and immediately stops all processing by terminating the program abnormally — no account records are read or written to any output file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Master File Open Failure Stops Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the Account Master File cannot be opened successfully, the program must immediately display an error message identifying the failure and halt all processing. No account records can be processed if the source file is unavailable.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has successfully opened the Account Input File and is preparing to process account records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Output Account File for writing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Output Account File must be opened and made ready to receive processed account records before any account processing begins

all_rules.Rule_Name: Output Account File Must Be Opened Before Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before any processed account records can be written, the sequential output account file must be successfully opened for writing. This ensures the destination file is ready to receive transformed account data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to open the Output Account File for writing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Output Account File opens successfully without any errors
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program marks the file operation as successful and continues to the next processing step, which is opening the Array Output File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Successful Output File Opening Allows Processing to Continue
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Output Account File is opened without any errors, the program is cleared to proceed to the next step in the account processing workflow.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to open the Output Account File for writing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Output Account File fails to open due to any error condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must: (1) display the error message 'ERROR OPENING OUTFILE' along with the file status indicator, (2) record the file status for diagnostic display, (3) display the detailed file status information, and (4) abnormally terminate the program to prevent further processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Failed Output File Opening Terminates Program with Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the Output Account File cannot be opened for writing, the program must immediately display an error message identifying the failure and terminate processing to prevent data loss or incomplete output.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has successfully opened the Account Input File and the Output Account File, and is now preparing to open the Array Output File for writing account balance array records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Array Output File for output
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Array Output File is successfully opened and the program proceeds to open the Variable Block Record Output File as the next step in the initialization sequence

all_rules.Rule_Name: Array Output File Must Be Available Before Account Processing Begins
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before any account balance array records can be written, the Array Output File must be successfully opened. This ensures the destination file is ready to receive account array data during processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is in the initialization phase and has attempted to open the Array Output File for writing account balance array records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Array Output File fails to open successfully due to any reason (e.g., file unavailable, access issue)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program displays the error message 'ERROR OPENING ARRAYFILE' along with the file status indicator, logs the file status for diagnostic purposes, and immediately stops all processing — no account records are read or written

all_rules.Rule_Name: Array Output File Unavailability Halts Account Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the Array Output File cannot be opened, the program must not proceed with any account record processing. An error message is displayed identifying the failed file, and the program is immediately terminated to prevent incomplete or missing array output data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has successfully opened the Account Input File, the Output Account File, and the Array Output File, and is now preparing to open the Variable-Length Record output file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Variable-Length Record output file for writing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file opens successfully, the program proceeds to begin reading and processing account records; no error is raised and processing continues normally

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Variable-Length Record Output File for Account Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before account processing begins, the program must open the Variable-Length Record output file. This file will store two types of account records (identity record and financial detail record) for every account processed. The file must be successfully opened before any account data can be written to it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to open the Variable-Length Record output file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file opens successfully without any errors
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program marks the operation as successful and continues to the main account processing loop where it will read, transform, and write account records across all output files

all_rules.Rule_Name: Successful Opening of Variable-Length Record File Allows Processing to Continue
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Variable-Length Record output file is opened without any issues, the program is cleared to proceed with account record processing. This is a prerequisite gate — all four files (Account Input, Output Account, Array, and Variable-Length Record) must be open before account processing begins.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to open the Variable-Length Record output file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file fails to open due to any error condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program displays the error message 'ERROR OPENING VBRC FILE' along with the file status details, and immediately terminates all processing — no account records are read or written

all_rules.Rule_Name: Failed Opening of Variable-Length Record File Stops Program Execution
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the Variable-Length Record output file cannot be opened, the program cannot proceed with account processing. An error message is immediately displayed identifying the failure, and the program is terminated. This ensures no partial or incomplete account data is processed without all required output destinations being available.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Master File is open for sequential reading and the end-of-file flag is set to 'N' (not yet reached end of file)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the next account record from the Account Master File and the record is successfully retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The account record is loaded into the Account Record working area, the processing result is marked as successful (OK), and the system proceeds to display, transform, and write the account record to all output files

all_rules.Rule_Name: Successful Sequential Read of Account Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account Master File is read sequentially and a valid account record is found, the system proceeds to process that account record through all downstream steps.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Master File is being read sequentially and all account records have already been processed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to read the next account record and the Account Master File signals that there are no more records (end-of-file condition is detected)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The processing result is marked as end-of-file, the end-of-file flag is set to 'Y', and the account processing loop is terminated — no further account records are read or processed

all_rules.Rule_Name: End-of-File Detection on Account Master File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the sequential read of the Account Master File reaches the end with no more records available, the system detects this condition and marks the end-of-file flag to stop the processing loop.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to read the next account record from the Account Master File and the end-of-file condition has been confirmed (no more records exist)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The end-of-file result is evaluated and confirmed as a valid end-of-file (not an error condition)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The end-of-file flag is set to 'Y', the main account processing loop detects this flag and stops iterating, and the program proceeds to the file closing and termination steps

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark End-of-File Flag to Stop Processing Loop
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the end-of-file condition is confirmed on the Account Master File, the system sets the end-of-file indicator to 'Y', which causes the main processing loop to exit and prevents any further attempts to read account records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been successfully read from the Account Master File and is available for processing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates the display of the account record details
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must display all of the following account fields in this exact sequence: (1) Account ID, (2) Account Active Status, (3) Current Balance, (4) Credit Limit, (5) Cash Credit Limit, (6) Account Open Date, (7) Account Expiration Date, (8) Account Reissue Date, (9) Current Cycle Credit Amount, (10) Current Cycle Debit Amount, (11) Group ID, and finally (12) a visual separator line to mark the end of the record display — all 12 display actions must be completed before returning to account processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Complete Account Record Details for Audit Trail
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account record is successfully read from the Account Master File, all account fields must be displayed in a defined sequence to provide a complete audit trail of the record being processed, followed by a visual separator line to distinguish between records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been successfully read from the Account Master File and contains a valid Account Reissue Date
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins preparing the Account Reissue Date for format conversion
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The original Account Reissue Date from the account record must be copied and preserved in working storage (WS-REISSUE-DATE) so it remains available for any subsequent processing that may require the unconverted date value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Preserve Original Account Reissue Date in Working Storage
all_rules.Rule_Description: When processing an account record, the original Account Reissue Date must be retained in working storage before any date conversion takes place, ensuring the source value is preserved for downstream use.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Reissue Date has been taken from the current account record and is ready for format conversion
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system configures the date conversion parameters
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The input date format type must be set to '2', indicating the format in which the Account Reissue Date is currently stored and will be submitted to the date formatting routine

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Input Date Format Type for Reissue Date Conversion
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before invoking the external date formatting routine, the input date format type must be explicitly set to type 2 to instruct the routine on how to interpret the incoming Account Reissue Date.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Reissue Date has been taken from the current account record and the input date format type has been set to '2'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system configures the output format parameter for the date conversion
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The output date format type must be set to '2', indicating the required format in which the converted Account Reissue Date should be returned by the date formatting routine

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Output Date Format Type for Reissue Date Conversion
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before invoking the external date formatting routine, the output date format type must be explicitly set to type 2 to instruct the routine on the required format for the converted Account Reissue Date.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been successfully read and contains a valid Account Reissue Date
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the date conversion input parameters
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Reissue Date from the account record must be copied into the date conversion input date field (CODATECN-INP-DATE) to serve as the source value for the external date formatting routine

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prepare Account Reissue Date as Input to Date Formatting Routine
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Reissue Date from the current account record must be placed into the date conversion input field so it can be submitted to the external date formatting routine for conversion.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Reissue Date has been placed in the date conversion input field, the input date format type is set to '2', and the output date format type is set to '2'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is ready to perform the date format conversion for the Account Reissue Date
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The external date formatting routine COBDATFT must be called with the complete date conversion record (containing the input date, input format type, and output format type) so that the routine can produce the correctly formatted Account Reissue Date

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invoke External Date Formatting Routine for Account Reissue Date
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must invoke the external date formatting routine COBDATFT to convert the Account Reissue Date from its current format (type 2) into the required output format (type 2), passing the full date conversion record containing the input date and both format type specifications.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The external date formatting routine COBDATFT has successfully converted the Account Reissue Date and returned the formatted date in the conversion output date field (CODATECN-OUT-DATE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system receives the formatted Account Reissue Date from the date formatting routine
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The formatted Account Reissue Date returned by COBDATFT must be moved into the output account record's Reissue Date field (OUT-ACCT-REISSUE-DATE), ensuring the output file contains the correctly formatted reissue date for the account

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Formatted Account Reissue Date into Output Account Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the external date formatting routine returns the converted Account Reissue Date, the formatted date must be stored in the output account record field so it is correctly represented in the output file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been read from the Account Master File and is being prepared for writing to the Output Account File, and the account's Current Cycle Debit Amount field is available for evaluation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account's Current Cycle Debit Amount is evaluated during output record population
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Current Cycle Debit Amount equals zero, the Output Record Current Cycle Debit field must be set to the default value of 2525.00; If the Current Cycle Debit Amount is any non-zero value, the Output Record Current Cycle Debit field must retain the original account Current Cycle Debit Amount unchanged

all_rules.Rule_Name: Apply Default Current Cycle Debit Value When No Debit Activity Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When processing an account record for output, if the account has no current cycle debit activity (i.e., the current cycle debit amount is zero), the system must assign a standard default debit value of 2525.00 to the output record's current cycle debit field. If a non-zero debit amount exists, the actual value is retained as-is in the output record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A source account record has been successfully read containing Account ID, Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Open Date, and Expiration Date
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The output account record is being populated from the source account record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following fields are copied directly and without transformation from the source account record to the output account record: Account ID, Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Open Date, and Expiration Date

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Core Account Fields to Output Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When populating the output account record, all core account identity and financial fields must be directly transferred from the source account record to the output record structure without modification.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A source account record contains an Account Reissue Date and the output account record is being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Reissue Date field is being mapped to the output record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Reissue Date is sent to the external date formatting program COBDATFT using input format type '2' and output format type '2', and the formatted result returned by COBDATFT is stored as the Reissue Date in the output account record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invoke External Date Formatter for Reissue Date Conversion
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Reissue Date must be converted to a standardized format by invoking the external date formatting service COBDATFT before it can be written to the output account record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The external date formatting program COBDATFT has successfully converted the Account Reissue Date
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The formatted date result is returned from the date formatter
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The formatted Reissue Date returned by COBDATFT is mapped to the Reissue Date field of the output account record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Formatted Reissue Date to Output Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the Reissue Date has been converted by the external date formatter, the formatted date result must be stored in the output account record's Reissue Date field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A source account record contains a Current Cycle Credit amount
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The output account record is being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Current Cycle Credit amount is copied directly from the source account record to the output account record without any transformation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Current Cycle Credit to Output Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Current Cycle Credit amount from the source account record must be directly transferred to the output account record without any modification.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A source account record is being processed and the Current Cycle Debit amount on the account is equal to zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Current Cycle Debit field is being mapped to the output account record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The output account record's Current Cycle Debit field is set to the default value of 2525.00 instead of zero

all_rules.Rule_Name: Apply Default Debit Value When Current Cycle Debit Is Zero
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account has no current cycle debit activity (i.e., the debit amount is zero), a system default debit value of 2525.00 must be applied to the output record instead of the zero value.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A source account record is being processed and the Current Cycle Debit amount on the account is not equal to zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Current Cycle Debit field is being mapped to the output account record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The actual Current Cycle Debit value from the source account record is copied directly to the output account record without any modification or default substitution

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Actual Current Cycle Debit When Non-Zero
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account has an existing non-zero current cycle debit amount, the actual debit value from the source account record must be carried forward to the output record as-is.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A source account record contains a Group ID and all other output account record fields have been populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The final field of the output account record is being mapped
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Group ID is copied directly from the source account record to the output account record, completing the population of the output account record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Group ID to Output Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Group ID from the source account record must be directly transferred to the output account record as the final step in populating the output record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A fully populated output account record is ready, containing all transformed account fields including Account ID, Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Open Date, Expiration Date, converted Reissue Date, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit (defaulted to 2525.00 if zero), and Group ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to write the populated account record to the sequential output file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The complete account record is successfully written to the sequential output file and processing continues to the next step

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Populated Account Record to Sequential Output File
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once all account fields have been populated and transformed, the complete account record must be written to the sequential output file to persist the processed data for downstream use.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A write operation has been attempted on the sequential output account file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The write operation results in any status other than a successful write or a normal end-of-file condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The output file write failure status is displayed on the console, the failure status details are logged, and the entire program is immediately terminated — no further account records are processed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Halt Processing on Output Account File Write Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the output account file write operation does not complete successfully, the program must immediately stop all processing to prevent incomplete or corrupted output data from being produced.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been successfully read from the Account Master File with a valid Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins populating the Account Balance Array Record for the current account
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Array Record Account ID field must be set to the same value as the current Account ID, establishing the link between the array record and its source account

all_rules.Rule_Name: Link Array Record to Account Identity
all_rules.Rule_Description: When building the account balance array record, the array record must be linked to the source account by copying the Account ID into the array record identifier field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been successfully read from the Account Master File with a valid Current Balance value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates Slot 1 of the Account Balance Array Record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Balance field in Slot 1 of the array record must be set to the exact value of the Account Current Balance from the source account record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Slot 1 Balance Reflects Actual Account Current Balance
all_rules.Rule_Description: The first balance slot in the account array record must carry the actual current balance of the account as read from the Account Master File.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is populating Slot 1 of the Account Balance Array Record for any account
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Current Cycle Debit field for Slot 1 is being assigned
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Current Cycle Debit field in Slot 1 of the array record must always be set to the fixed standard value of 1005.00, irrespective of the account's actual debit balance

all_rules.Rule_Name: Slot 1 Carries a Fixed Standard Debit Amount of 1005.00
all_rules.Rule_Description: The first debit slot in the account array record must always carry a fixed, predetermined debit amount of 1005.00, regardless of any actual account debit activity.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been successfully read from the Account Master File with a valid Current Balance value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates Slot 2 of the Account Balance Array Record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Balance field in Slot 2 of the array record must be set to the exact value of the Account Current Balance from the source account record, identical in source to Slot 1's balance

all_rules.Rule_Name: Slot 2 Balance Reflects Actual Account Current Balance
all_rules.Rule_Description: The second balance slot in the account array record must also carry the actual current balance of the account, mirroring the same source value used in Slot 1.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is populating Slot 2 of the Account Balance Array Record for any account
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Current Cycle Debit field for Slot 2 is being assigned
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Current Cycle Debit field in Slot 2 of the array record must always be set to the fixed standard value of 1525.00, irrespective of the account's actual debit balance

all_rules.Rule_Name: Slot 2 Carries a Fixed Standard Debit Amount of 1525.00
all_rules.Rule_Description: The second debit slot in the account array record must always carry a fixed, predetermined debit amount of 1525.00, regardless of any actual account debit activity.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is populating Slot 3 of the Account Balance Array Record for any account
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Balance field for Slot 3 is being assigned
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Balance field in Slot 3 of the array record must always be set to the fixed negative value of -1025.00, regardless of the account's actual current balance

all_rules.Rule_Name: Slot 3 Carries a Fixed Negative Standard Balance of -1025.00
all_rules.Rule_Description: The third balance slot in the account array record must always carry a fixed negative balance of -1025.00, representing a standard adjustment or reversal entry, independent of the account's actual current balance.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is populating Slot 3 of the Account Balance Array Record for any account
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Current Cycle Debit field for Slot 3 is being assigned
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Current Cycle Debit field in Slot 3 of the array record must always be set to the fixed negative value of -2500.00, regardless of the account's actual current cycle debit

all_rules.Rule_Name: Slot 3 Carries a Fixed Negative Standard Debit Amount of -2500.00
all_rules.Rule_Description: The third debit slot in the account array record must always carry a fixed negative debit amount of -2500.00, representing a standard adjustment or reversal debit entry, independent of the account's actual debit activity.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account balance array record has been fully populated with the account ID, three balance slots, and three corresponding debit amounts for the current account being processed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to write the populated array record to the Array Output File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The array record is successfully written to the Array Output File and processing returns to the main account processing loop to continue with the next account record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Populated Account Balance Array Record to Array Output File
all_rules.Rule_Description: For each account processed, the populated array record containing multiple balance and debit entries must be successfully written to the Array Output File. If the write operation fails, processing must be halted immediately.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to write an account balance array record to the Array Output File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The write operation results in any status other than a successful write or normal end-of-file condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the error message 'ACCOUNT FILE WRITE STATUS IS:' along with the specific write failure status received, displays the detailed file status information, and immediately stops all program processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Halt Processing on Array Output File Write Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the write of the account balance array record to the Array Output File does not complete successfully, the program must immediately stop all processing. This ensures data integrity by preventing partial or incomplete array output file records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been successfully read from the Account Master File and contains a valid Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the short variable-length record (12-byte identity record)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID from the source account record is copied exactly into the Account ID field (VB1-ACCT-ID) of the short variable-length record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Copy Account ID to Short Variable-Length Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When building the short variable-length record for an account, the Account ID from the source account record must be copied into the Account ID field of the short record (VB1). This ensures the short record is correctly identified by its account.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been successfully read from the Account Master File and contains a valid Account Active Status
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the short variable-length record (12-byte identity record)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Active Status from the source account record is copied exactly into the Active Status field (VB1-ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS) of the short variable-length record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Copy Account Active Status to Short Variable-Length Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When building the short variable-length record for an account, the Account Active Status from the source account record must be copied into the Active Status field of the short record (VB1). This ensures the short record carries the current activation state of the account.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been read from the Account Master File and both Account ID and Account Active Status have been populated into the short record fields (VB1-ACCT-ID and VB1-ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The short variable-length record is ready to be written to the variable-length record output file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The short record contains exactly two data elements — Account ID and Account Active Status — and is structured as a 12-byte record before being written to the variable-length record output file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Short Variable-Length Record Structure Definition
all_rules.Rule_Description: The short variable-length record written to the variable-length record output file is defined as a fixed 12-byte record containing exactly two fields: Account ID and Account Active Status. This record serves as a compact identity record for each account processed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid account record has been successfully read from the Account Master File and contains an Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the long variable-length record (VB2) for the current account
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID from the source account record is copied exactly as-is into the Account ID field of the long variable-length record VB2

all_rules.Rule_Name: Copy Account ID to Long Variable-Length Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When building the long variable-length record (VB2), the Account ID from the source account record must be carried over as the primary identifier of the long record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid account record has been successfully read from the Account Master File and contains a Current Balance value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the long variable-length record (VB2) for the current account
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Current Balance from the source account record is copied exactly as-is into the Current Balance field of the long variable-length record VB2

all_rules.Rule_Name: Copy Current Balance to Long Variable-Length Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When building the long variable-length record (VB2), the account's current balance must be included to capture the real-time financial standing of the account.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid account record has been successfully read from the Account Master File and contains a Credit Limit value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the long variable-length record (VB2) for the current account
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Credit Limit from the source account record is copied exactly as-is into the Credit Limit field of the long variable-length record VB2

all_rules.Rule_Name: Copy Credit Limit to Long Variable-Length Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When building the long variable-length record (VB2), the account's credit limit must be included to capture the maximum credit authorized for the account.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid account record has been successfully read from the Account Master File and contains a Reissue Date from which the four-digit year (YYYY) has been extracted into the working storage reissue year field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the long variable-length record (VB2) for the current account
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Only the four-digit Reissue Year (YYYY) — not the full reissue date — is copied into the Reissue Year field of the long variable-length record VB2

all_rules.Rule_Name: Copy Reissue Year to Long Variable-Length Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When building the long variable-length record (VB2), only the four-digit year (YYYY) portion of the account's reissue date is extracted and stored, not the full reissue date.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All four fields — Account ID, Current Balance, Credit Limit, and Reissue Year (YYYY) — have been populated into the long variable-length record (VB2) for the current account
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The long variable-length record VB2 is prepared for writing to the variable-length record output file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The long variable-length record VB2 is assembled as exactly 39 bytes in length, containing Account ID, Current Balance, Credit Limit, and Reissue Year in that defined structure, and is ready to be written as the second of two variable-length records for the account

all_rules.Rule_Name: Long Variable-Length Record VB2 Structure and Size Definition
all_rules.Rule_Description: The long variable-length record (VB2) is a defined 39-byte record structure that consolidates four key account data elements — Account ID, Current Balance, Credit Limit, and Reissue Year — into a single output record written to the variable-length record output file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been successfully read and its identity fields (Account ID and Active Status) have been populated into the short variable-length record structure
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to write the short variable-length record to the variable-length record output file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The record length indicator must be set to exactly 12 bytes prior to placing the record content into the output buffer

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Record Length for Short Variable-Length Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before writing the short account identity record to the variable-length record file, the record length must be explicitly set to 12 bytes to ensure correct sizing of the output record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The record length has been set to 12 bytes and the short variable-length record (VB Record 1) contains the Account ID and Account Active Status for the current account being processed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system loads the output buffer in preparation for writing to the variable-length record file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The short account identity record (containing Account ID and Active Status) must be copied into exactly the first 12 bytes of the variable-length record output buffer, and no other fields should be included in this record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Output Buffer with Short Account Identity Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The short account identity record, containing Account ID and Active Status, must be placed into the first 12 bytes of the output buffer before writing to the variable-length record file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The 12-byte output buffer has been populated with the short account identity record containing Account ID and Active Status
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the write operation to the variable-length record output file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The 12-byte record must be successfully written to the variable-length record output file, and the system must proceed to write the second variable-length record (39-byte detail record) for the same account

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Short Variable-Length Record to Output File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The 12-byte short account identity record, loaded into the output buffer, must be written to the variable-length record output file as the first of two variable-length records produced per account.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to write the 12-byte short account identity record to the variable-length record output file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The write operation completes and the file status is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the write is successful, the system must continue processing by writing the second variable-length record (39-byte detail record) for the same account; If the write is unsuccessful, the system must display the message 'ACCOUNT FILE WRITE STATUS IS:' along with the file status code, display the detailed file status information, and immediately stop all processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Successful Write of Short Variable-Length Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: After writing the short variable-length record, the system must verify the write operation completed successfully. If the write fails, account processing must be halted immediately to prevent incomplete or corrupted output.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been successfully read from the Account Master File and contains a valid Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the 39-byte long variable-length record for writing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID from the source account record is copied into the Account ID field of the long variable-length record (VB Record 2)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Account ID to Long Variable-Length Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account ID from the source account record must be mapped to the long variable-length record (VB Record 2) before writing to the variable-length record file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been successfully read from the Account Master File and contains a Current Balance value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the 39-byte long variable-length record for writing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Current Balance from the source account record is copied into the Current Balance field of the long variable-length record (VB Record 2)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Current Balance to Long Variable-Length Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Current Balance from the source account record must be mapped to the long variable-length record (VB Record 2) before writing to the variable-length record file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been successfully read from the Account Master File and contains a Credit Limit value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the 39-byte long variable-length record for writing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Credit Limit from the source account record is copied into the Credit Limit field of the long variable-length record (VB Record 2)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Credit Limit to Long Variable-Length Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Credit Limit from the source account record must be mapped to the long variable-length record (VB Record 2) before writing to the variable-length record file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been successfully read from the Account Master File and contains an Account Reissue Date with a year component
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the 39-byte long variable-length record for writing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Only the year portion (YYYY) of the Account Reissue Date is extracted from the working storage reissue date and copied into the Reissue Year field of the long variable-length record (VB Record 2)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Reissue Year to Long Variable-Length Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: Only the year portion of the Account Reissue Date from the source account record must be extracted and mapped to the long variable-length record (VB Record 2) before writing to the variable-length record file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The long variable-length record (VB Record 2) has been fully populated with Account ID, Current Balance, Credit Limit, and Reissue Year
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is ready to write the long variable-length record to the variable-length record file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The record length is set to exactly 39 bytes, and the populated VB Record 2 content is placed into the first 39 bytes of the variable-length record buffer

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Fixed Record Length of 39 Bytes for Long Variable-Length Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The long variable-length record (VB Record 2) containing account financial details must always be assigned a fixed length of 39 bytes before being written to the variable-length record file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The long variable-length record (VB Record 2) has been fully populated with Account ID, Current Balance, Credit Limit, and Reissue Year, and the record length has been set to 39 bytes
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system writes the 39-byte long variable-length record to the variable-length record file (VBRC-FILE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The 39-byte record is successfully written to the variable-length record file, and processing continues to the next step; if the write operation does not complete successfully, the system displays an account file write status error message and terminates processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write 39-Byte Long Variable-Length Record to Variable-Length Record File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The fully populated 39-byte long variable-length record containing account ID, current balance, credit limit, and reissue year must be written to the variable-length record output file (VBRC-FILE) for every account processed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Master File has been successfully opened and contains zero or more account records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to read the next account record from the Account Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If a valid account record is returned, it is made available for further processing; if the end-of-file condition is detected (no more records exist), the loop terminates and all-accounts-processed is flagged as complete

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Account Records Until All Accounts Are Processed
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program continuously reads account records one at a time from the Account Master File and processes each record. The loop repeats until all account records have been read and the end-of-file condition is reached.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid account record has been successfully read from the Account Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account record is available for processing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following eleven account fields are displayed on the console: Account ID, Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Open Date, Expiration Date, Reissue Date, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, and Group ID, followed by a separator line

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Account Record Details on Console
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each account record successfully read from the Account Master File must be displayed on the console with all key account fields before any transformation or output processing begins.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid account record has been read and the Account Reissue Date is available from the Account Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The output account record is being prepared for writing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Reissue Date is passed to the external date conversion routine (COBDATFT) with input format type 2 and output format type 2, and the converted date is stored as the output Account Reissue Date; additionally, the original reissue date is preserved in a working storage field for later use in variable-length record population

all_rules.Rule_Name: Convert Account Reissue Date Format
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Reissue Date must be converted from its source format to the required output format using the standard date conversion service before being written to the output account file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid account record has been read from the Account Master File and the output account record is being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account Current Cycle Debit field on the input account record is equal to zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The output Account Current Cycle Debit is set to the default value of 2525.00 instead of the zero value from the source record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Apply Default Current Cycle Debit When Zero
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account has no current cycle debit activity (zero debit amount), a standard default debit value must be applied to the output record to ensure the output account file always contains a meaningful cycle debit value.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid account record has been read from the Account Master File and the reissue date conversion has been completed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The output account record is being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following fields are copied directly from the source account record to the output account record: Account ID, Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Open Date, Expiration Date, Current Cycle Credit, and Group ID; the Reissue Date is populated with the converted date value; the Current Cycle Debit is populated with the source value if non-zero, or with the default value of 2525.00 if the source value is zero

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Output Account Record Fields
all_rules.Rule_Description: All fields from the source account record are mapped to the output account record, with the reissue date replaced by its converted value and the current cycle debit subject to a default rule.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The output account record has been fully populated with all required fields including the converted reissue date and the applicable current cycle debit value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The write operation is performed to the Output Account File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The complete output account record is successfully written to the Output Account File and processing continues to populate the array record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Populated Record to Output Account File
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the output account record has been fully populated with all transformed fields, it must be written to the Output Account File.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid account record has been read and the output account record has been written to the Output Account File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account balance array record is being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID is set from the source account record; Slot 1 is populated with the Account Current Balance as the balance and a fixed debit amount of 1005.00; Slot 2 is populated with the Account Current Balance as the balance and a fixed debit amount of 1525.00; Slot 3 is populated with a fixed balance of -1025.00 and a fixed debit amount of -2500.00 regardless of the actual account data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Account Balance Array Record with Three Fixed Slots
all_rules.Rule_Description: For every account processed, an array record containing three balance and debit slots must be created. Slots 1 and 2 carry the actual account current balance with predetermined fixed debit amounts, while Slot 3 always carries fixed negative values representing a standard adjustment entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account balance array record has been fully populated with Account ID and three balance and debit slots
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The write operation is performed to the Array Output File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The complete array record is successfully written to the Array Output File and processing continues to populate the variable-length records

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Account Balance Array Record to Array Output File
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the three-slot account balance array record has been populated, it must be written to the Array Output File.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid account record has been read and the array record has been written to the Array Output File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The variable-length records are being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The short variable-length record (Record 1) is populated with Account ID and Account Active Status; the long variable-length record (Record 2) is populated with Account ID, Current Balance, Credit Limit, and the Reissue Year (year portion only, extracted from the working storage reissue date field); both records are displayed on the console before being written

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Short and Long Variable-Length Records
all_rules.Rule_Description: For every account processed, two variable-length records must be prepared: a short identity record containing account identification and status, and a long financial detail record containing account financial information including the reissue year.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The short variable-length record has been populated with Account ID and Account Active Status
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The short record write operation is performed to the Variable-Length Record File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The short record content is placed into the first 12 bytes of the variable-length record buffer and the record is written to the Variable-Length Record File with a length of 12 bytes

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Short Identity Record to Variable-Length File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The short identity variable-length record containing Account ID and Active Status must be written to the Variable-Length Record File with a defined length of 12 bytes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The long variable-length record has been populated with Account ID, Current Balance, Credit Limit, and Reissue Year, and the short record has already been written to the Variable-Length Record File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The long record write operation is performed to the Variable-Length Record File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The long record content is placed into the first 39 bytes of the variable-length record buffer and the record is written to the Variable-Length Record File with a length of 39 bytes; processing then returns to the loop to read the next account record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Long Financial Detail Record to Variable-Length File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The long financial detail variable-length record containing Account ID, Current Balance, Credit Limit, and Reissue Year must be written to the Variable-Length Record File with a defined length of 39 bytes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All account records from the Account Master File have been read and processed successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initiates the closure of the Account Master File

description:
CBACT01C is a batch COBOL program in the CardDemo application that reads account records sequentially from an indexed account file and writes the data into multiple output files. For each account record read, it populates and writes a formatted account record to a sequential output file, an array-based record to an array file, and two variable-length records to a variable-length record file. The program also performs date formatting by calling an external assembler routine (COBDATFT) and applies specific business rules such as defaulting the current cycle debit to 2525.00 when it is zero.
- **Execution Environment**: Batch - **Database Access**: VSAM (Indexed), Sequential Files - **MQ Calls**: No - **Module Type**: Main/Driver Program
### Key Functionalities: 1: Open Account File - Open the indexed account master file in sequential read mode to begin processing all account records 2: Open Output Account File - Open the sequential output file where processed account records will be written 3: Open Array Output File - Open the sequential array file where account balance array records will be written 4: Open Variable-Length Record File - Open the sequential variable-length record file where two types of account records will be written 5: Read Next Account Record - Sequentially read the next account record from the indexed account master file and detect end-of-file condition 6: Display Account Record Details - Display all fields of the current account record including account ID, active status, current balance, credit limit, cash credit limit, open date, expiration date, reissue date, current cycle credit, current cycle debit, and group ID 7: Format Account Reissue Date - Call external date formatting routine (COBDATFT) to convert the account reissue date into the required output format 8: Apply Default Cycle Debit Value - If the account current cycle debit amount is zero, assign a default value of 2525.00 to the output record 9: Populate Output Account Record - Map all account fields (ID, active status, current balance, credit limit, cash credit limit, open date, expiration date, formatted reissue date, current cycle credit, current cycle debit, group ID) to the output account record structure 10: Write Output Account Record - Write the fully populated account record to the sequential output file 11: Populate Account Balance Array Record - Build an array record for the account containing the account ID and five balance slots: slot 1 with current balance and fixed debit of 1005.00, slot 2 with current balance and fixed debit of 1525.00, slot 3 with fixed balance of -1025.00 and fixed debit of -2500.00 12: Write Account Balance Array Record - Write the populated array record containing multiple balance entries to the array output file 13: Populate Short Variable-Length Record - Build a short account record (12 bytes) containing account ID and active status for writing to the variable-length record file 14: Populate Long Variable-Length Record - Build a long account record (39 bytes) containing account ID, current balance, credit limit, and reissue year for writing to the variable-length record file 15: Write Short Variable-Length Record - Write the 12-byte variable-length record containing account ID and active status to the variable-length record file 16: Write Long Variable-Length Record - Write the 39-byte variable-length record containing account ID, current balance, credit limit, and reissue year to the variable-length record file 17: Process All Accounts Loop - Repeatedly read and process each account record from the account master file until all records have been processed (end-of-file reached) 18: Close Account File - Close the account master file after all records have been processed
